Standard Cu/SHE galvanic cell
With [Cu²⁺] = 1 M, H₂ at 1 atm, and H⁺ at 1 M, the voltmeter reads the standard cell potential, +0.337 V.

plan.contextChunk: This figure shows a galvanic cell used to measure the standard electrode potential for the Cu2+/Cu half-reaction, consisting of a standard hydrogen electrode (SHE) on the left connected via a salt bridge and voltmeter to a copper half-cell on the right, all operating at T = 298 K. The left beaker contains a 1 M H+ solution into which the SHE — a platinum electrode with 1 atm H2(g) bubbling past it — is immersed, and curved arrows near the electrode indicate the anode half-reaction 2H+ + 2e− → H2 running in reverse (oxidation). The right beaker contains a 1 M Cu2+ solution with a copper metal electrode (Cu electrode) immersed in it, and a curved arrow from Cu2+ to Cu indicates the cathode half-reaction Cu2+(aq) + 2e− → Cu(s). An inverted-U-shaped salt bridge connects the two beakers to complete the ionic circuit, while the external wire carries electron flow (shown by arrows) from the SHE anode to the Cu cathode, passing through a digital voltmeter that reads +0.337 V. This figure establishes the experimental method for determining standard electrode potentials by referencing an unknown half-cell against the SHE and demonstrates that the Cu2+/Cu couple has a standard reduction potential of +0.337 V.

interactions.label: [Cu²⁺] concentration / M
interactions.teaches: Changing the copper ion concentration changes the cell voltage according to the Nernst equation; at 1 M the cell reads the standard value +0.337 V, while lower or higher Cu²⁺ shifts the potential below or above that value

interactions.label: Animate electron and ion flow
interactions.teaches: Electrons travel through the external wire from anode to cathode, while ions move through the salt bridge to maintain charge neutrality and complete the circuit

interactions.label: Cell direction
interactions.teaches: Reversing which half-cell is the cathode reverses the spontaneous direction of electron flow and flips the sign of the measured voltage

demo_steps.title: Standard Cu/SHE galvanic cell
demo_steps.narration: With [Cu²⁺] = 1 M, H₂ at 1 atm, and H⁺ at 1 M, the voltmeter reads the standard cell potential, +0.337 V. Electrons flow from the standard hydrogen electrode to the copper electrode.

demo_steps.title: Lower copper ion concentration
demo_steps.narration: Reducing [Cu²⁺] makes copper reduction less favorable, so the Nernst equation lowers the voltage below +0.337 V.

demo_steps.title: Higher copper ion concentration
demo_steps.narration: Increasing [Cu²⁺] makes copper reduction more favorable, raising the measured potential above the standard value.

demo_steps.title: Reverse the cell
demo_steps.narration: Swapping anode and cathode reverses the electron-flow arrows and changes the voltmeter reading to the opposite sign for the same chemical conditions.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Use a flat front-on schematic layout matching the source. Overall scene spans about 12 world units wide by 8 units high. Left beaker centered at x=-3.2, y=-1.4; right beaker centered at x=3.2, y=-1.4. Each beaker is a transparent glass cylinder-like outline about 3.0 units wide and 3.2 units tall, with a slightly flared lip, gray-blue glass stroke #9fb2bb at about 35% opacity and pale highlights. Solutions fill the lower 2.25 units: left H+ solution pale blue #bfeeff at about 55% opacity; right Cu2+ solution brighter cyan #32c7f4 at about 70% opacity. Liquid surfaces are white/cyan ellipses about 2.7 units wide. SHE on the left sits just left of the beaker center: vertical glass tube from y=-3.0 to y=1.8, narrow transparent cylinder about 0.55 units wide, with a side gas inlet entering from the left at y=0.8. Platinum wire is a thin dark gray vertical line at x=-3.55 from y=1.7 to y=-2.3; platinum plate is a dark gray rectangle about 0.35 × 0.65 units at bottom. Hydrogen bubbles are small white circles rising in the left solution near x=-4.0 to -2.8. Copper electrode in right beaker is a vertical orange-brown strip at x=4.25, from y=1.25 down to y=-2.6, about 0.55 units wide, colored #d97850 with darker #b85535 edges and diagonal highlight streaks. Salt bridge is an inverted U tube: left end dips into left beaker at x=-1.9, y=-2.0; rises to y=1.75; arches across to right; right end dips into right beaker at x=2.25, y=-2.0. Draw as thick translucent tube, pale lavender-gray #dbe2f2 with opacity 0.55, outer stroke about 0.55 units wide and inner highlight. External wire is thick black #000000, starting from SHE wire at x=-3.55, y=1.8, rising and curving to the voltmeter, then from voltmeter to the copper electrode at x=4.25, y=1.25. Voltmeter centered at x=0, y=3.6, size about 2.2 × 0.75 units, rounded rectangle black/gray body with green LCD #d8efaa. Display text should show E in volts to three decimals, including sign: for normal direction E = 0.337 + (0.05916/2) log10([Cu2+]); for reversed direction E = -0.337 - (0.05916/2) log10([Cu2+]). Assume T=298 K, n=2, [H+] = 1 M, PH2 = 1 atm. Top electron-flow arrows in normal direction point left-to-right along the wire; reversed mode points right-to-left. In normal mode label left half-cell as anode and right as cathode; oxidation at SHE: H2(g) -> 2H+ + 2e−, reduction at copper: Cu2+ + 2e− -> Cu(s). In reversed mode swap labels, reverse curved half-reaction arrows, and reverse electron particles.
interactionPlan.notes: Render as a clean layered 2D/2.5D Three.js scene using transparent shapes and tube curves, not a physically exact glass simulation. Use CSS2D or SDF text for labels so chemical notation supports superscripts/subscripts. Animate electrons as small yellow or white dots moving along a sampled CatmullRomCurve path on the external wire; in normal mode move from the left electrode through the voltmeter to the right electrode. Animate salt-bridge ions as small colored particles: anions migrate toward the left anode in normal mode, cations toward the right cathode; reverse directions when the cellDirection toggle is reversed. Update voltmeter text and the right bottom concentration label whenever the slider changes. Use logarithmic perceptual handling for the concentration slider if available, but keep the displayed value in molarity.

plan.authoredInteractions:
- Slider for Cu2+ ion concentration: watch the voltmeter reading update in real time as the Nernst equation shifts the cell potential above or below the standard value of positive 0.337 V
- Animate the electron and ion flow: show electrons moving from the standard hydrogen electrode through the external wire to the copper electrode, and ions migrating through the salt bridge to balance charge
- Toggle to swap which half-cell is the cathode and which is the anode: reverse the cell and show the voltmeter sign flipping

authoredContext:
This approach to measuring electrode potentials is illustrated in , which depicts a cell comprised of an SHE connected to a copper(II)/copper(0) half-cell under standard-state conditions. A voltmeter in the external circuit allows measurement of the potential difference between the two half-cells. Since the Cu half-cell is designated as the cathode in the definition of cell potential, it is connected to the red (positive) input of the voltmeter, while the designated SHE anode is connected to the black (negative) input. These connections insure that the sign of the measured potential will be consistent with the sign conventions of electrochemistry per the various definitions discussed above. A cell potential of +0.337 V is measured, and so

Tabulations of E° values for other half-cells measured in a similar fashion are available as reference literature to permit calculations of cell potentials and the prediction of the spontaneity of redox processes.

A cell permitting experimental measurement of the standard electrode potential for the half-reaction Cu 2+ ( a q ) + 2 e − ⟶ Cu ( s )

This figure contains a diagram of an electrochemical cell. Two beakers are shown. Each is just over half full. The beaker on the left contains a clear, colorless solution and is labeled below as “1 M H superscript plus.” The beaker on the right contains a blue solution and is labeled below as “1 M C u superscript 2 plus.” A glass tube in the shape of an inverted U connects the two beakers at the center of the diagram. The tube contents are colorless. The ends of the tubes are beneath the surface of the solutions in the beakers and a small graylug is present at each end of the tube. The beaker on the left has a glass tube partially submersed in the liquid. Bubbles are rising from the gray square, labeled “Standard hydrogen electrode” at the bottom of the tube. A curved arrow points up to the right, indicating the direction of the bubbles. A black wire extends from the gray square up the interior of the tube through a small port at the top to a rectangle with a digital readout of “positive 0.337 V,” which is labeled “Voltmeter.” A second small port extends out the top of the tube to the left. An arrow points to the port opening from the left. The base of this arrow is labeled “1 a t m H subscript 2 ( g ).” The beaker on the right has an orange-brown strip that is labeled “C u electrode” at the top. A wire extends from the top of this strip to the voltmeter. An arrow points toward the voltmeter from the left which is labeled “e superscript negative flow.” Similarly, an arrow points away from the voltmeter to the right. A curved arrow extends from the surrounding solution to the standard hydrogen electrode in the beaker. The end of the arrow is labeled “H subscript 2” and tip of this arrow is labeled “2 H superscript plus.” A curved arrow extends from the “C u superscript 2 plus” label in the solution to a “C u” label at the lower edge of the C u electrode. Between the two beakers is the label “T equals 298 K.”

provides a listing of standard electrode potentials for a selection of half-reactions in numerical order, and a more extensive alphabetical listing is given in Appendix L .

discrepancies: Extra colored ion/electron particles and added Anode/Cathode polarity labels are visible even though the source figure only shows arrows and chemical labels.
The H2 gas inlet area is crowded and partially confused by overlapping arrow/tube/label geometry compared with the clean source arrow and label.
Glass beakers, salt bridge, and electrode proportions are simplified and less like the original detailed textbook illustration, especially the salt bridge and beaker rims.
The copper half-cell reaction arrow/labels are lower and closer to the electrode than in the source, changing the visual balance of the right beaker.
The generated figure is lighter and more schematic than the source, with weaker glass outlines and less faithful shading/detail.
evaluation.notes: The main Cu/SHE galvanic cell is recognizable and chemically accurate, but the added particles/polarity labels and some simplified/crowded drawing details reduce textbook fidelity.
action_items: Remove or hide the extra ion/electron particles and Anode/Cathode labels by default to better match the source figure.
Clean up the H2 inlet arrow and label so the arrowhead, tube, and text do not visually collide.
Adjust beaker, salt bridge, and electrode proportions/shading to more closely match the source illustration.
Reposition the Cu2+/Cu reaction labels and curved arrow to match the original right-beaker layout.
